key_insight: MedPsy’s compact medical language models combine strong benchmark performance with shorter responses and lower on-device resource use.
clinical_relevance: These models could support local medical-language applications on laptops and smartphones, but the reported results do not establish clinical safety or patient benefit.
method: Train 1.7B and 4B text-only models using synthetic medical data and reasoning targets from a 235B teacher.
Apply two supervised fine-tuning stages followed by two reinforcement-learning stages with hard-sample mining.
Evaluate GGUF quantization variants and real-device inference on laptop and smartphone hardware.
evidence_signal: Across seven closed-ended medical benchmarks, MedPsy-4B matched MedGemma-27B; on HealthBench-Hard it scored 15.33 points higher, while device tests reported 75% lower median latency and estimated energy per answer versus its Qwen3 backbone at matched quantization.
watch_item: Benchmark and tested-device results do not establish reliability in clinical workflows; prospective validation and device-specific testing remain necessary.
paper_title: MedPsy: State-of-the-Art Small Medical Language Models for Efficient Edge Deployment
